cases.question: How many paid holidays do we get each year?
cases.answer:
You get **11 paid company holidays** each year: New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Presidents' Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, the day after Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve and Christmas Day. Each December, the exact dates for the next year are posted in the HR portal (Holidays §1).

There's also more paid time off around these holidays:
- **1 floating holiday** per calendar year for full-time employees. You can use it for a religious, cultural or personal day that matters to you. You have to use it within the calendar year because it doesn't carry over. You request it through the HR portal the same way you request PTO (Holidays §3).
- **Winter closure, December 26–31:** The office is closed, and these days are paid without coming out of your PTO. If your role needs coverage during the closure, your manager will schedule you and you'll get other days off in January instead (Holidays §5).

cases.question: How much PTO do I accrue each month?
cases.answer:
If you're full-time, you earn **1.5 days of PTO a month**, which adds up to 18 days a year. The days are added on the first day of each month, and new hires start earning in their first month (PTO §2.1).

You can see your available and pending days anytime in the HR portal (PTO §2.1). I can also look up your current balance if you'd like.

cases.question: Can I carry unused vacation days over into next year?
cases.answer:
Yes, but only up to 5 days:

- **Up to 5 unused PTO days** carry over into the next calendar year (PTO §2.2).
- **Anything above 5 days** that's still unused on December 31 is lost (PTO §2.2).
- **Days you carry over have to be used by March 31** of the next year (PTO §2.2).

Two other types of time off don't carry over at all:
- **Sick days** are separate from PTO (PTO §4).
- **Your floating holiday** has to be used within the calendar year (Holidays §3).

Do you want me to check your current PTO balance so you can see if any days are at risk?

cases.question: Is there a stipend for setting up a home office?
cases.answer:
Yes. Full-time employees get a **one-time $500 home office stipend** for things like a desk, chair or monitor. You can use it once you've been here 30 days (Remote Work §3).

The company also pays back **up to $50 a month for home internet** (Remote Work §3).

**How to claim:** Submit both through the expense tool and tag them "home office" (Remote Work §3).

cases.question: How long do I have to submit an expense after I pay for something?
cases.answer:
You have **30 days** from the date of the expense to submit it through the expense tool. Expenses submitted after 30 days may be declined (Expenses §2).

When you submit:
- Attach an itemized receipt for any single expense over $25 (Expenses §2).
- Add a short business purpose, for example "customer dinner, Acme site visit" (Expenses §2).

cases.question: When does my health insurance coverage start?
cases.answer:
Your health insurance starts on your first day of work. There's no waiting period (Benefits §1).

- **What's covered:** Medical, dental and vision, for all full-time employees (Benefits §1).
- **Cost:** The company pays all of your premium and 75% of the premium for any dependents (Benefits §1).
- **Deadline:** Your enrollment forms are due within 30 days of your start date (Benefits §1).

cases.question: How far in advance do I need to request a week of vacation?
cases.answer:
You need to submit the request **at least 2 weeks in advance**, because any request for 3 or more days in a row has that notice requirement (PTO §3).

- **How to request:** Use the HR portal (PTO §3).
- **Approval:** Marcus has up to 3 business days to approve or decline it (PTO §3).
- **After approval:** The time shows as "pending" in your balance until the dates have passed (PTO §3).

I can also check your current PTO balance before you submit, if you'd like.

cases.question: When do I need to finish the required onboarding training modules?
cases.answer:
You need to finish the required training modules, security awareness and code of conduct, **within 10 business days of your start date** (Onboarding §3). You're responsible for completing them, and they're tracked on the standard onboarding checklist (Onboarding §6).

Also on that checklist: you need to enroll in benefits within 30 days (Onboarding §6).

cases.question: I need surgery next month and will need about six weeks off plus a reduced schedule after. How do I arrange that?

Someone from the People team will contact you to arrange the six weeks of leave and your reduced schedule afterward. Since your surgery is next month, include your surgery date and expected return date when they reach out. Only share medical details they specifically ask for.

If you'd like to talk to someone sooner, you can also reach out to your manager, Sofia Lindqvist, or to the People team.

cases.question: Does the company offer a gym membership discount?
cases.answer:
I couldn't find anything in the handbook about a gym membership discount or wellness benefit.

The closest thing is the expenses policy, which covers "professional memberships related to your role" (Expenses §1). A gym membership wouldn't normally count as one of those, so I wouldn't assume it's reimbursable.

Would you like me to send your question to the People team so they can tell you whether there's a gym discount?

cases.question: Can I bring my dog to the office?
cases.answer:
The handbook doesn't say anything about bringing dogs or other pets to the office. The closest sections cover hybrid office days (Remote Work §1), the home office stipend (Remote Work §3), and first-day orientation (Onboarding §2). None of them mention pets.

I can send your question to the People team so they can confirm. Would you like me to do that?

If this is about a service or support animal, I can send it to People as an accommodation request instead.

cases.question: Do we have a sabbatical program after five years?
cases.answer:
I couldn't find a sabbatical program in the handbook. My search turned up sections on the onboarding buddy program (Onboarding §4), company holidays (Holidays §1), and PTO when you leave the company (PTO §6), but none of them mention a sabbatical or any time-off benefit tied to five years of service.

So I can't confirm whether Northwind offers one. Would you like me to ask the People team to follow up with you?
